name: 01 · Cybersecurity verb forms · Normal
description: 30 preguntas SOC para practicar formas verbales con frases útiles para clientes, incidentes y explicación del trabajo del SOC.

questions.question: Before we start, I need to ___ a few details with you.
questions.explanation: Después de “need to” usamos V1: confirm. Formas: confirm – confirmed – confirmed – confirming.
questions.translation: Antes de empezar, necesito confirmar algunos detalles contigo.

questions.question: We can ___ the affected account as soon as you approve the action.
questions.explanation: Después del modal “can” usamos V1 sin “to”: isolate. Formas: isolate – isolated – isolated – isolating.
questions.translation: Podemos aislar la cuenta afectada en cuanto apruebes la acción.

questions.question: Please ___ the incident number in the subject line.
questions.explanation: El imperativo usa V1: include. Formas: include – included – included – including.
questions.translation: Por favor, incluye el número de incidente en el asunto.

questions.question: We did not ___ any signs of data exfiltration during the initial review.
questions.explanation: Después de “did not” usamos V1: find, no “found”. Formas: find – found – found – finding.
questions.translation: No encontramos indicios de exfiltración de datos durante la revisión inicial.

questions.question: Our next step is to ___ the endpoint logs with the proxy logs.
questions.explanation: Después de “to” usamos V1: compare. Formas: compare – compared – compared – comparing.
questions.translation: Nuestro siguiente paso es comparar los logs del endpoint con los del proxy.

questions.question: Let me ___ what the SOC has done so far.
questions.explanation: La estructura “let + persona + verbo” lleva V1: let me explain. Formas: explain – explained – explained – explaining.
questions.translation: Déjame explicar lo que ha hecho el SOC hasta ahora.

questions.question: The customer asked us to ___ an interim update every two hours.
questions.explanation: La estructura “ask someone to + verbo” lleva V1 tras “to”: provide. Formas: provide – provided – provided – providing.
questions.translation: El cliente nos pidió que proporcionáramos una actualización provisional cada dos horas.

questions.question: We must ___ the evidence before we close the case.
questions.explanation: Después de “must” usamos V1 sin “to”: preserve. Formas: preserve – preserved – preserved – preserving.
questions.translation: Debemos preservar las evidencias antes de cerrar el caso.

questions.question: Yesterday, we ___ the suspicious domain at the firewall.
questions.explanation: “Yesterday” indica pasado terminado, así que usamos V2: blocked. Formas: block – blocked – blocked – blocking.
questions.translation: Ayer bloqueamos el dominio sospechoso en el firewall.

questions.question: The analyst ___ the customer as soon as the severity increased.
questions.explanation: La acción ocurrió en un momento pasado terminado; usamos V2: called. Formas: call – called – called – calling.
questions.translation: El analista llamó al cliente en cuanto aumentó la severidad.

questions.question: During the call, the user ___ that they had opened the attachment.
questions.explanation: Para narrar lo que ocurrió en la llamada usamos V2: said. Formas irregulares: say – said – said – saying.
questions.translation: Durante la llamada, el usuario dijo que había abierto el archivo adjunto.

questions.question: At 10:15, the team ___ the compromised host offline.
questions.explanation: La hora pasada concreta exige V2: took. Formas irregulares: take – took – taken – taking.
questions.translation: A las 10:15, el equipo desconectó el host comprometido.

questions.question: The monitoring rule ___ three new alerts last night.
questions.explanation: “Last night” marca un periodo pasado y terminado; usamos V2: generated. Formas: generate – generated – generated – generating.
questions.translation: La regla de monitorización generó tres alertas nuevas anoche.

questions.question: The attacker ___ a credential-dumping tool before we isolated the server.
questions.explanation: En la narración del incidente usamos V2 para esta acción pasada: ran. Formas irregulares: run – ran – run – running.
questions.translation: El atacante ejecutó una herramienta de volcado de credenciales antes de que aisláramos el servidor.

questions.question: We ___ with the customer about the containment plan during yesterday’s bridge call.
questions.explanation: “Yesterday’s bridge call” sitúa la acción en el pasado terminado; usamos V2: spoke. Formas: speak – spoke – spoken – speaking.
questions.translation: Hablamos con el cliente sobre el plan de contención durante la llamada de coordinación de ayer.

questions.question: We have ___ the updated report to all stakeholders.
questions.explanation: Después de “have” usamos V3: sent. Formas irregulares: send – sent – sent – sending.
questions.translation: Hemos enviado el informe actualizado a todas las partes interesadas.

questions.question: The analyst has ___ the root cause in the executive summary.
questions.explanation: Después de “has” usamos V3: written, no V2 “wrote”. Formas: write – wrote – written – writing.
questions.translation: El analista ha escrito la causa raíz en el resumen ejecutivo.

questions.question: The affected server has been ___ out of production.
questions.explanation: En “has been + participio” necesitamos V3: taken. Formas: take – took – taken – taking.
questions.translation: El servidor afectado se ha retirado de producción.

questions.question: We have ___ no evidence of persistence on the isolated host.
questions.explanation: Después de “have” usamos V3: found. Formas: find – found – found – finding.
questions.translation: No hemos encontrado evidencias de persistencia en el host aislado.

questions.question: The customer has ___ us permission to reset the credentials.
questions.explanation: Después de “has” usamos V3: given, no V2 “gave”. Formas: give – gave – given – giving.
questions.translation: El cliente nos ha dado permiso para restablecer las credenciales.

questions.question: The same indicator has been ___ on three endpoints.
questions.explanation: La pasiva de present perfect usa “has been + V3”: seen. Formas: see – saw – seen – seeing.
questions.translation: El mismo indicador se ha observado en tres endpoints.

questions.question: The attacker had ___ several tools on the server before we isolated it.
questions.explanation: Después de “had” usamos V3: left. Formas irregulares: leave – left – left – leaving.
questions.translation: El atacante había dejado varias herramientas en el servidor antes de que lo aisláramos.

questions.question: We are ___ the authentication logs while we speak.
questions.explanation: El present continuous se forma con “are + -ing”: reviewing. Formas: review – reviewed – reviewed – reviewing.
questions.translation: Estamos revisando los logs de autenticación mientras hablamos.

questions.question: The team is ___ a timeline for the customer update.
questions.explanation: Después de “is” usamos la forma -ing para una acción en curso: building. Formas: build – built – built – building.
questions.translation: El equipo está elaborando una cronología para la actualización al cliente.

questions.question: The sensor is ___ normally again after the restart.
questions.explanation: El present continuous usa “is + -ing”: running. “Run” duplica la consonante final: run – ran – run – running.
questions.translation: El sensor vuelve a funcionar con normalidad después del reinicio.

questions.question: I am ___ the main findings on my screen now.
questions.explanation: Después de “am” usamos la forma -ing: showing. Formas: show – showed – shown – showing.
questions.translation: Estoy mostrando ahora los principales hallazgos en mi pantalla.

questions.question: The SOC is ___ the customer’s infrastructure team during containment.
questions.explanation: Para una actividad que está ocurriendo usamos “is + -ing”: supporting. Formas: support – supported – supported – supporting.
questions.translation: El SOC está apoyando al equipo de infraestructura del cliente durante la contención.

questions.question: The malware was caught while ___ to contact its command-and-control server.
questions.explanation: Después de “while” podemos usar la forma -ing para una acción simultánea: trying. Formas: try – tried – tried – trying.
questions.translation: El malware fue detectado mientras intentaba contactar con su servidor de mando y control.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have wrote the incident report.
We have written the incident report.
We have writing the incident report.
We have write the incident report.
questions.explanation: Después de “have” necesitamos V3. La forma correcta es written: write – wrote – written – writing.
questions.translation: Hemos escrito el informe del incidente.

questions.question: During yesterday’s call, I ___ with the customer; since then, I have ___ with their network team twice.
questions.explanation: La primera acción usa V2 por “yesterday”: spoke. Después de “have” usamos V3: spoken. Formas: speak – spoke – spoken – speaking.
questions.translation: Durante la llamada de ayer hablé con el cliente; desde entonces, he hablado dos veces con su equipo de red.
